_note: The parts of speech to look up (/gramatica/classes-de-palavras) and Regi's line under the part-of-speech label of the flashcards (wortschatz-app.js). `practice` = the anchor of the exercise on /parts-of-speech where the class comes up. `fehler` = the word pair on /gramatica/erros-comuns that belongs to the class, empty where none fits. `id` = the pos field in the lexicon; the article has no lexicon word of its own but belongs here. `examples` are set by hand (European Portuguese, A1) so the page does not depend on the lexicon. `say` is the short form for the card (≤ 8 words), `what` the sentence on the page, `tr` its translation into the help languages (`en` = the same sentence; the other languages were removed on 2026-11-13 where `what` changed for Portuguese and come back with the UI-language items).

classes.name: Noun
classes.say: A noun is a name for something.
classes.what: A noun is a name: for a person, an animal, a thing or an idea.
classes.tip: Every Portuguese noun is masculine or feminine: o livro, a casa. Most nouns have a plural: livro – livros. Names of people and places start with a capital letter: Amina, Lisboa.

learn.label: Nouns and gender: rule and exercises

tr.en: A noun is a name: for a person, an animal, a thing or an idea.

classes.name: Article
classes.say: An article comes before a noun.
classes.what: An article comes before a noun and agrees with it: o, a, os, as for a thing we both know; um, uma, uns, umas for one of many, or some.
classes.ask: o or a? um or uma?
classes.tip: The article shows the gender and the number: o carro, a casa, os carros, as casas. a, de, em and por join with the article: vou ao banco, venho do banco, moro no Porto, passo pela Junta.

learn.label: Articles: o, a, um, uma – rule and exercises

tr.en: An article comes before a noun and agrees with it: o, a, os, as for a thing we both know; um, uma, uns, umas for one of many, or some.

classes.name: Verb
classes.say: A verb says what someone does.

sub.name: pronominal verb
sub.what: A verb that comes with a pronoun: levanto-me, lembras-te, vai-se embora.

classes.what: A verb says what someone does or what happens.
classes.ask: What does he do? What happens?
classes.tip: The ending shows the person, so the pronoun is often left out: falo, falas, fala. The infinitive ends in -ar, -er, -ir (or is pôr): falar, comer, partir.

tr.en: A verb says what someone does or what happens.

classes.name: Adjective
classes.say: An adjective says what something is like.
classes.what: An adjective says what someone or something is like.
classes.tip: An adjective agrees with its noun and usually goes after it: uma casa branca, uns carros brancos. Some have one form for both genders: um andar grande, uma casa grande.

tr.en: An adjective says what someone or something is like.

classes.name: Adverb
classes.say: An adverb says when, where or how.
classes.what: An adverb says when, where or how something happens.
classes.tip: Adverbs don't change their form. Many end in -mente: rapidamente, normalmente. Others don't: hoje, aqui, sempre, bem.

tr.en: An adverb says when, where or how something happens.

classes.name: Pronoun
classes.say: A pronoun stands for a noun.
classes.what: A pronoun stands for a noun, so you don't have to repeat it.
classes.tip: A Ana chega tarde. → Ela chega tarde, or just: Chega tarde. Vejo a Ana. → Vejo-a.

tr.en: A pronoun stands for a noun, so you don't have to repeat it.

classes.name: Preposition
classes.say: A preposition comes before a noun: a, en, de.
classes.what: A preposition comes before a noun and shows place, time or direction.
classes.tip: After a preposition, use a noun, a pronoun or an infinitive: com o meu amigo, para ti, antes de sair. Many join with the article: de + o = do, em + a = na.

tr.en: A preposition comes before a noun and shows place, time or direction.

classes.name: Conjunction
classes.say: A conjunction joins words and sentences.
classes.what: A conjunction joins words or sentences.
classes.tip: e, ou and mas join two sentences: Estou cansado, mas vou. porque gives a reason. Careful: e = and, é = is.

tr.en: A conjunction joins words or sentences.

classes.name: Number
classes.what: A number word says how much or how many, or in which position.
classes.ask: How many? How much? Which one in order?
classes.tip: dois filhos (how many?), o segundo dia (which one in order?). um becomes uma before a feminine noun: um livro, uma casa; dois becomes duas: duas casas.

tr.en: A number word says how much or how many, or in which position.

classes.name: Phrase
classes.also: not a part of speech, a fixed group of words
classes.say: A phrase: several words, one meaning.
classes.what: A phrase is several words that together have one fixed meaning.
classes.tip: Learn it as a whole. Translated word for word, it often doesn't work: Está tudo bem?

tr.en: A phrase is several words that together have one fixed meaning.
